vanderhoeven1868_p111-112_source-note.pn.note: Van der Hoeven's own source statement for Bijlagen XVIII-XXIX: the documents come from 'het stedelijk archief van Breda' (the Breda TOWN archive, not the Hague Staten-Generaal archive), consisting of Havermans' diary (Bijlage XVIII) and 'brieven en rapporten van den magistraat aan de Prinsen Maurits en Frederik Hendrik en de antwoorden daarop ontvangen, voor 't grootste gedeelte in cijferschrift' (letters and reports from the magistrate to the Princes and the answers received, for the most part in cipher). P.112 continues with the Bijlage XX story specifically: the key to that incoming cipher letter was found only after much effort, by a secretary of Spinola -- i.e. that letter's cipher was originally unbroken by Breda itself and had to be solved by the besieging Spanish side.
